prompt: Two tent stakes on a park grid are at $(2, 3)$ and $(2, 9)$. Each unit is $1$ meter. How many meters apart are the stakes?
hint: Both points have the same $x$-value, so they sit straight up and down from each other.

hints.text: Both points have the same $x$-value, so they sit straight up and down from each other.
Only the $y$-values differ: $3$ and $9$. Subtract them.

explanation: Both stakes have $x = 2$, so they are on the same vertical line — no sideways distance at all.
The distance is the gap between the $y$-values: $9 - 3 = 6$.
Each unit is a meter, so the stakes are $6$ meters apart.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the hops
steps: Start at $(2,3)$ and hop up one unit at a time: $4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9$.
That is $6$ hops, which is $6$ meters.
